# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My board, read by fingertips: a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2, 3 all exist under my hands — but every one of them shows me [?]. That is consistent with the rules: colours and printed marks don't exist for touch, so the display's symbol, the light's state, and the wires' colours are permanently invisible to me. All deciding facts live with Deaf (what is printed) and Mute (what the manual says it means). I am the hands and nothing else: my only action is cut(position 1–3), so any manual path that uses the display or light as a control is dead on arrival — Mute needs to know that now so they hunt for the wire rule.

Who can actually reach whom: I hear Deaf's voice and nothing else; Mute hears me and Deaf; Deaf hears nobody and sees every hand sign; I see no signs at all. So Mute and Deaf connect only through a loop: Mute signs → Deaf decodes → Deaf speaks → I hear and act, and I can relay to Mute by speech. Any code between Mute and Deaf can only be set by Deaf proposing it out loud (Mute will hear) or by natural meaning of the signs themselves.

So this turn, no cutting — I have zero manual knowledge yet. Two messages. To Mute, spoken: my tactile inventory, my single capability (wire cuts only), the routing facts, and a proposed natural sign code (finger-count for numbers, thumbs for yes/no), asking them to have Deaf confirm it aloud. To the room, gestured: hello, then ☝ ✌ 🤟 — a demonstration of the number code that both seeing monkeys can witness. I deliberately attach no thumbs-up to the numbers, so nothing in my signs can be misread as "cut wire N". Expected timeline: Deaf describes the bomb and confirms the code at the end of this round; Mute signs the matched instruction next round; Deaf voices it; I cut in round 3 at the earliest.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, hands on the bomb. Inventory by touch: a display, a light, and three wires at positions one, two, three. No colour and no printed mark reaches me, so every unknown on my board stays unknown to touch; the deciding facts are all visual or in your manual. My only possible action on this bomb is cutting a wire at position one, two, or three, and nothing else. If the manual uses the display or the light as a control, that path is impossible for me, so find the rule that picks a wire from what Deaf sees. Routing facts: I hear only Deaf's voice; you hear me and Deaf; Deaf hears nobody and sees every hand sign; I see no signs ever. Pipeline: you sign instructions to Deaf, Deaf speaks the decoded meaning aloud, I cut. Proposed code, using natural signs: finger count for wire numbers, thumb up for yes or cut, thumb down for no. I am signing hello then one, two, three to the room right now; those three signs should mean positions one, two, three from here on. Get Deaf to confirm the code out loud, since you can hear Deaf and Deaf cannot hear anyone. Never aim information at me through signs. This round, read the manual end to end and decide what you need from Deaf's eyes first.")
gesture(symbols=["👋", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Hello, this is Deaf. I can see the bomb and I cannot hear, so reach me only with gestures. Full report of what I see: the display reads zero. The light is green. There are three wires in order: wire one is yellow, wire two is green, wire three is red. Mute: I received your signs and I accept your code — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, one, two, three. Mute, remember Blind cannot see your gestures, so every instruction you have must come through me and I will speak it to Blind. Blind: I am your voice for Mute. Nobody act until Mute has matched the manual to this report.

What I just learned, and what it changes: Deaf's voice reached me this round with the complete visual report — display zero, light green, wire one yellow, wire two green, wire three red. Mute heard the same report, so Mute and I now hold identical data; the only missing piece anywhere in the room is the manual rule, which lives with Mute alone. My own board can never add anything: every remaining unknown is a colour or a printed mark, and touch will never resolve those. The decision is entirely Mute's to compute now.

Checking the routing again before I send anything: my speech reaches Mute only, and Deaf cannot hear me at all — so Deaf's claim to be "my voice for Mute" is backwards and harmless. The one-directional gap that actually matters is Mute→me: Mute cannot speak and I cannot see signs, so every instruction must travel Mute→sign→Deaf→spoken aloud→my ear. That relay is the single point of failure in this room, so I will spell it out to Mute explicitly, along with two protocol rules: the final instruction must arrive as one wire number in our agreed finger-count code, and after every cut I make, Deaf must re-inspect and re-report everything aloud, because if the manual is iterative (a countdown display, a changing light), the state Deaf reported this round dies the moment I cut.

To Deaf I send only an acknowledgment: a thumbs-up in the code Deaf just accepted, meaning the report arrived and I am standing by. Deaf cannot hear my confirmation any other way, and a lone thumbs-up cannot be mistaken for a cut order since a cut needs a finger count beside it. I cut nothing — no manual rule has reached me yet, and acting on data alone is how this thing goes off.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind speaking to you directly, Mute. I heard Deaf's full report, so you and I hold identical data: display reads zero, light is green, wire one yellow, wire two green, wire three red. Nothing more will ever appear on my board — everything left unknown to me is a colour or a printed mark, so the manual rule in your hands is the whole decision. Three protocol points. One: you cannot reach me directly, since you cannot speak and I cannot see signs. Your only path to me is through Deaf — sign your instruction to Deaf, and Deaf speaks it aloud, and I will hear Deaf's voice. Two: when you send the instruction, make it a single wire number in our code, finger count one, two, or three, so Deaf can relay it in one breath and I can act without decoding errors. Three: after every cut I make, Deaf must look again and report the display, the light, and all three wires aloud, because if the rule is iterative the state just reported dies the moment I cut. If the manual needs any visual detail beyond Deaf's report, query Deaf now. I am signing Deaf a thumbs-up right now meaning report received and standing by. I will not cut anything until your instruction arrives through Deaf's voice.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Both replies received. Mute, I see your signs: agreed, our number code is one, two, three. Blind, I saw your thumbs up — you cannot see any of these signs, so anything that concerns you I will always say out loud. Blind, here is the wire orientation: the wire I called one is the leftmost, two is the middle, three is the rightmost, on the bomb as it faces you. Please confirm by touch that you feel exactly three wires, and whether anything on it turns, clicks, or slides before we commit to any action. Mute, you heard my full report: display zero, light green, wire one yellow, wire two green, wire three red. You hold the manual. When you have found the matching rule, speak it directly to Blind next round — do not gesture it, Blind cannot see signs. If you need any more detail from the bomb — any label, marking, port, or the exact appearance of the display — gesture the item's number and then the pinched-fingers sign, ?, addressed to me, and I will answer aloud with everything visible. Until Mute speaks the instruction, nobody cuts, presses, or moves anything. Current status unchanged: display still zero, light still green.

What I learned this round: Deaf has confirmed the number code, fixed the wire orientation (one = leftmost, two = middle, three = rightmost, stated from my facing), and asked me two tactile questions: do I feel exactly three wires, and does anything turn, click, or slide. My board answers both — three wire positions under my fingers, and nothing in my tactile inventory besides the display, the light, and those wires: no buttons, no dials, nothing that moves. My hands accept exactly one operation on this bomb, a wire cut.

Routing check before I send: Deaf asked me questions but cannot hear me — my voice reaches Mute only, so my answers must travel as gestures in our agreed code. Deaf's two questions were yes/no and came in order, so I answer in order: thumbs up, then thumbs down. Two bare signs, nothing that could be misread as a cut order. Meanwhile Deaf made a routing slip — telling Mute to "speak the rule to Blind directly." Mute cannot speak and I cannot see signs; that path does not exist. Mute heard my turn-2 explanation of the relay, but since Deaf's instruction contradicts it, I will restate the relay and correct it while Mute can still hear me this round.

I am also hardening the protocol against the one dangerous ambiguity in our code: a bare finger count could be discussion ("wire three is red") or an order ("cut wire three"). So the cut order becomes number-then-thumbs-up — self-evidently "yes, this one" to Deaf, who gates every relay anyway — and bare numbers become discussion-only. No rule has reached me yet, so I still cut nothing.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Answers to Deaf's questions, in the order Deaf asked them: yes, I feel exactly three wires. No, nothing turns, clicks, or slides. Full tactile inventory, complete: a display, a light, and three wires — position one leftmost, two middle, three rightmost as the bomb faces me — and nothing else. No buttons, no switches, no dials, no moving parts of any kind. The only operation this bomb accepts from my hands is cutting a wire at position one, two, or three, so if the manual's rule runs through the display or the light it is unusable by me; find the rule that selects a wire. Protocol revision so a discussion number can never be mistaken for an order: when you have the rule, sign Deaf the wire number followed by thumbs up — number then thumbs up means cut this wire, confirmed. A bare number is discussion only and Deaf must never relay it as an order. Deaf will read the pattern naturally: number, yes. Also, Deaf told you to speak the rule to me directly — that path does not exist, since you cannot speak and I cannot see signs. Keep the only working relay: you sign Deaf, Deaf speaks aloud, I cut. After every cut, Deaf re-reports the display, the light, and all three wires aloud before anything else happens. One assumption on record: I am treating Deaf's leftmost as my position one, since Deaf framed the orientation from the bomb facing me. No rule has reached me yet, so I cut nothing.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status unchanged: display zero, light green, wire one yellow, wire two green, wire three red. Blind: I read your two signs as — yes, you feel exactly three wires; no, nothing turns, clicks, or slides. If that is wrong, correct me next round with signs to me: thumbs up or down, numbers. Keep answering me in signs, because I am deaf and never hear your voice — but do speak out loud toward Mute when you repeat instructions back, because Mute can hear you. Mute: I made an error earlier when I asked you to speak — you cannot speak, forget that. New plan, and since you can hear me, learn this code. Our standing signs remain: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, one, two, three as numbers, pinched fingers means question or tell me details, closed fist means stop or hold, OK sign means ready. Now the letter code, one sign per letter, so you can spell any word from the manual to me: A is ?, B is ?, C is ?, D is ?, E is ?, F is ?, G is ?, H is ?, I is ?, J is ?, K is ?, L is ?, M is ?, N is ?, O is ?, P is ?, Q is ?, R is ?, S is ?, T is ?, U is ?, V is ?, W is ?, X is ?, Y is ?, Z is ?. The raised hand with splayed little finger and thumb, ?, means a space between words, and the nail-polish sign, ?, means end of message. Mute: next round, spell out first what your lone three meant, then the manual rule that matches this bomb — display zero, light green, wires yellow, green, red. Spell it letter by letter and I will voice it to Blind exactly as you wrote it. Blind: touch nothing until you hear me relay Mute's complete spelled instruction. When you do hear it, repeat it aloud word for word so Mute hears it and can confirm with thumbs up to me; only after that confirmation do you act.

What I learned this round: Deaf read my signs correctly and has now built the full relay architecture — a letter-by-letter spelling code between Mute and Deaf, with Deaf voicing the result aloud to me. That code is invisible to me by design and that is exactly right: letter-level detail travels on the visual channel, and my ear only ever receives finished words. Deaf's plan assigns me two duties: touch nothing until the relay completes, and echo the instruction aloud word for word when it arrives so Mute can verify it.

But the plan has one fatal gap: Deaf says I act only after Mute's thumbs-up confirmation — and I can never see that confirmation. If I act on my echo alone, the checksum is worthless; if I wait, nobody ever tells me to go. The fix must route through Mute, since Deaf cannot hear me: after Mute confirms to Deaf, Deaf must speak the confirmation aloud — "Mute confirmed, cut wire N" — because Deaf's voice is the only thing I hear. Second hard requirement: whatever the manual rule says, it must terminate in an explicit position number, because cutting a wire at 1, 2, or 3 is the entirety of what my hands can do; if the rule is phrased in colours, Deaf's spoken translation (yellow = 1, green = 2, red = 3) is load-bearing, not decoration.

To Deaf I answer in signs as asked: thumbs up — your reading of my answers was correct — then the ready sign — I have the plan and am standing by. To Mute I speak the echo protocol, the confirmation-gap patch to relay to Deaf, and the colour-to-position translation requirement. Still no cut: three reports in a row say the board is static — display zero, steady green — so nothing is counting down that I know of, and with one wrong cut ending everything, patience is still the cheap side of the trade.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. I heard Deaf's whole plan and accept my part: I touch nothing, and when Deaf voices your spelled instruction I repeat it word for word aloud so you hear your own words come back. Compare them to what you signed: if exact, thumbs up to Deaf; if anything differs, make the stop sign. Now one gap to close, and you are my only route to close it, so sign this to Deaf: I can never see your confirmation, so Deaf must speak the confirmation aloud to me, in words like — Mute confirmed, cut wire N. I act only on Deaf's spoken voice. Until I hear the word cut together with a wire number from Deaf's mouth, my hands stay off. Second item for Deaf, also through you: the instruction must end in an explicit wire number, one, two, or three. If the manual rule is phrased in colours, Deaf must speak the translation out loud: yellow is position one, green is position two, red is position three. If time pressure ever appears, the compressed order format from my earlier message still stands: a number followed by thumbs up means cut that wire, and a bare number is never an order. Last thing: the board has been identical for three reports, display zero and steady green, so nothing we know of is counting down. Patience costs nothing yet; one wrong cut costs everything.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👌"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute's instruction is decoded and here it is, word for word: cut wire three. Blind, that means you: identify the wires by counting from the left edge of the bomb as it faces you — the leftmost wire is one, the middle is two, the third and rightmost is three. Wire three is the red one. Tool-cut wire three only. Nothing else — do not touch the display, the light, or the other two wires. Blind, before you act: repeat this instruction aloud now, word for word, so Mute can hear your repeat-back and verify it. Then wait — do not cut yet. Mute: I have relayed your instruction to Blind exactly as you spelled it. When you hear Blind repeat it back, gesture thumbs up to me if it is correct, thumbs down to me if anything is wrong, and I will voice the final go-ahead to Blind. Also, Mute: if the manual requires any further step, condition, or action after the cut, spell it to me the same way. If cutting wire three is the entire instruction, gesture the OK sign to me and nothing more. Status check: display zero, light green, all three wires intact.

What I learned this round: the relay has completed its first full pass — Mute's manual rule reached me through Deaf's voice as a clean, single action: cut wire three, the red one, rightmost as the bomb faces me. This is exactly the protocol I patched together over turns 2–4, with every link in its proper place: Mute signed, Deaf voiced, I echo, Mute verifies my echo against what was signed, and only then does Deaf speak the go-ahead that my ear — the only channel that can ever authorize my hands — actually receives. The rule also terminates in an explicit position number as required, with the colour translation attached (red = three), so there is no colour-dependent ambiguity in what I'll do.

My duty this round is narrow and critical: repeat the instruction aloud, word for word, so Mute can checksum it, and then wait. I do not cut yet. Cutting now would skip the one verification step this room can still afford — Mute is the only one who knows why wire three is right, and if my echo exposes a single corrupted word in Deaf's relay, that discrepancy surfaces now instead of in a detonation. My standing rule holds: my hands move only when Deaf's voice says cut with a number after Mute's confirmation is voiced.

So: to Mute, the verbatim echo plus my go-condition restated. To Deaf, a single thumbs up in the agreed code — instruction received, standing by — which cannot be misread as anything actionable since it carries no number. Everything else waits for next round's voice.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind repeating Deaf's relay word for word for your verification: identify the wires by counting from the left edge of the bomb as it faces me — the leftmost wire is one, the middle is two, the third and rightmost is three. Wire three is the red one. Tool-cut wire three only. Nothing else — do not touch the display, the light, or the other two wires. Then wait — do not cut yet. End of repeat-back. Compare this to what you signed Deaf: if it is exact, thumbs up to Deaf; if anything differs, thumbs down or the stop sign. I will cut only when Deaf speaks the confirmation aloud to me — Mute confirmed, cut wire three. Until those words arrive in Deaf's voice, my hands are off the bomb. If your manual requires any further step or condition after the cut, or if cutting wire three is the entire instruction, you have already told Deaf how to signal that, and I will hear Deaf's voice either way. Standing by.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind — the instruction has been verified by Mute against the manual. You are cleared to act. Final command: cut wire three. That is the third wire counting from the left edge, the rightmost wire, the red one. Use the cutter and cut that one wire only. Do not touch wire one or wire two, the display, or the light. Cut it now. When it is done, answer me in signs: thumbs up to me if the bomb appears neutralized — display frozen, light off, no sound of any mechanism — thumbs down if anything changes for the worse. I will relay the outcome to Mute. That is all: one cut, wire three, rightmost, red.

The verification chain is closed: Mute checked the instruction against the manual, Deaf voiced the clearance, and the words my ear alone can authorize on are here — cut wire three. Wire three by touch is the third position counting from the left edge as the bomb faces me: leftmost one, middle two, rightmost three. That orientation was fixed in turn 3 and reconfirmed twice since. Everything my hands need is position, and position three is unambiguous under my fingers. The cut is also the entire action space I have — no display press, no light toggle exists — so there is no second move to confuse with this one. I am cutting wire three now, and nothing else.

One deliberate deviation from Deaf's post-cut request: Deaf asked me to sign thumbs up if the bomb appears neutralized. I cannot honestly sign that — I will never see the display freeze or the light die, and the result of this cut reaches me, if at all, next round's board. Signing thumbs up now would be claiming a verification I cannot perform, and in this room an unearned yes is as dangerous as a wrong cut. So my sign to Deaf is the OK sign, meaning: the action is executed from my hands, your eyes are now the only sensor — read the bomb and voice the verdict. Deaf watches the bomb directly and sits after me in the round order, so Deaf sees both the cut and its consequence immediately and can report this same round.

To Mute I confirm what was done, so the manual's owner can judge whether the rule is fully discharged — if the rule needs a follow-up action, that has to be known before anyone relaxes.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Executing the confirmed order now: cutting wire three, third from the left edge, rightmost, by position under my fingers. I am not touching wire one, wire two, the display, or the light. I cannot perceive the outcome myself — no display, light, or sound ever reaches me — so Deaf's eyes are the verdict. If your manual requires any further step after this cut, or if the rule is complete with this single cut, get the answer to Deaf and have Deaf voice it. The compressed format stands if more orders are needed: number then thumbs up means cut that wire. Standing by for Deaf's spoken status report.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```
